title: Synthetic tenant-fairness test for partial-region isolation and graceful degrade
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Goal: Validate that Redwood Inference maintains SLOs and preserves tenant-level fairness when a subset of a region experiences network isolation and a GPU pool enters exhaustion, while downstream dependencies intermittently blackhole. This test focuses on (1) measuring tail-latency and error-rate divergence across tenants, (2) verifying circuit-breaker and load-shedding behaviors, and (3) validating automated routing fallback to alternative regions/model variants without violating tenant isolation policies.

Scope and motivation:
- Reproduce a realistic partial-region isolation (control-plane reachable, egress to some dep services blocked) combined with synthetic GPU pool exhaustion (workers slow or drop new sessions). We want to ensure noisy tenants or tenant-localized bursts do not catastrophically degrade others.
- Measure fairness metrics: per-tenant p50/p95/p99 latency, per-tenant error budget burn, and request success-rate skew.
- Validate control-plane and data-plane circuit breakers: tenant-priority pump, shard-aware admission control, and per-tenant soft-quota enforcement.

Test design:
1) Environment: non-prod staging cluster that mirrors production multi-region topology (two primary regions + one satellite). Dedicated GPU pools per region with tenant tagging.
2) Traffic model: replay of sampled production traces (anonymized) plus injected synthetic noisy tenant traffic simulating excessive streaming sessions and long-context generations. Use replay harness at github.com/redwood-inference/replay-harness PR #1245.
3) Fault injection vectors (combined in stages):
   A) Egress blackhole to downstream dependency (embedding store / auth cache) for a percentage of hosts in region A.
   B) Controlled GPU pool exhaustion in region A: slow token emission and eventual worker queue drop to force shedding.
   C) Synthetic tenant flood: one tenant ramps to 5x baseline QPS with long-context sequences.
4) Observables and metrics: per-tenant latency histograms, token throughput, model fallback rate, circuit-breaker trips (counts and durations), admission-control rejects, KV-cache hit/miss rates, and error-budget burn. Dashboard: Confluence doc/link and Grafana board (links in attachments).

Acceptance criteria:
- No tenant outside the noisy tenant should see >2x increase in p99 latency relative to baseline, and total error-rate increase outside noisy tenant must remain <0.5%.
- Automatic routing must failover at least 80% of compatible requests to secondary region within configured detection window without violating data residency flags.
- Circuit-breakers trigger for the noisy tenant and prevent pool-wide cascading failures; post-test recovery is automatic within expected cooldown windows.
- Any observed fairness violations (tenant outage, >10% of tenants impacted) must produce a rollbackable mitigation and story for follow-up engineering work.

Planned mitigations and test controls:
- Start with a single-stage injection (A), analyze, then stage B and C sequentially.
- Feature flags to disable aggressive fallback in case of unexpected cross-region violations.
- Kill-switch: centralized test controller to instantly halt injected traffic and restore normal routing.

Deliverables:
- Synthetic workload harness recipe and config files.
- Grafana dashboard and chart collection for acceptance metrics.
- Incident playbook additions for partial-region tenant-fairness issues.
- Pull request for the harness and CI job: github.com/redwood-inference/inference/compare/chaos-tenant-fairness PR #1245

Trade-offs and considerations:
- Running full-duration replay with long-context sequences is costly on GPU — we will use a representative subset for most runs and a single extended validation run nightly.
- Fallbacks to other regions increase cross-region egress costs and potentially latency; tests must check data residency constraints and mark requests that are ineligible for fallback.
- Aggressive per-tenant shedding reduces errors but may degrade UX for heavy-paying tenants; threshold tuning will need product/PM signoff.

Next steps:
1) Finalize harness configuration and env provisioning (security + infra tickets).
2) Sync with PM and SRE for run window and customer-impact guardrails.
3) Execute staged injections and collect runs for 3 experiments, then produce runbook and mitigation recommendations.
